FY27 consolidated revenue guided at ₹2,000 Cr with 14-15% EBITDA; Garmenting division at 15%.
FY27 machine base: 5,700 in India, 2,000 in Sri Lanka and 1,400 in Young Brand; no FY28 expansion decided.
Order book about ₹600 Cr: ₹380 Cr SPAL Garmenting, ₹142 Cr Young Brand, GBP 6.1 million SPUK.
Retail needs equity to become PAT-positive; finance cost, not depreciation, is the drag.
Labour has not fully returned after capacity was cut; management expects only 30-40% to come back and is rehiring.
UK and EU FTAs expected in the next 2-3 months; management says benefits would go to customers as more orders, not higher prices.

timeline.summary: P. Sundararajan, as promoter, declared no new encumbrances on S. P. Apparels Limited shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) for FY2025-26 on 02.04.2026.
On April 21, 2026, S. P. Apparels invested ₹6.32 Cr as equity in its UK wholly owned subsidiary S.P Apparels UK P Limited.
P. Sundararajan, promoter of S. P. Apparels Limited, declared no new encumbrances by promoters or promoter group for FY2025-26 on 02.04.2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹364.91 Cr, net profit ₹18.59 Cr (-38.8% YoY).
On 22 May 2026 S.P. Apparels' Q4/FY26 earnings call kept FY27 guidance at ₹2,000 Cr consolidated revenue and 14-15% EBITDA, with Sri Lanka targeted at ₹200-250 Cr and recovery pushed to H2FY27.
S.P. Apparels held Q1FY27 earnings call on August 13, 2026, reaffirming FY27 revenue guidance of ₹2,000 Cr and announcing dividend and stock split

watchlist.response: CFO pointed to current utilisation of only 64% in Indian factories and said 100% sales will come from existing factories and Sri Lanka; MD said all the lift happens in H2.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on how the ₹2,000 Cr FY27 target is reached when Sri Lanka and Sivakasi add only about ₹250-300 Cr to FY26's ₹1,578 Cr.
